The run will make a best effort to use only the number of prompt tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run. If the run exceeds the number of prompt tokens specified, the run will end with status `incomplete`. See `incomplete_details` for more info.

model.description: The ID of the [Model](/docs/api-reference/models) to be used to execute this run. If a value is provided here, it will override the model associated with the assistant. If not, the model associated with the assistant will be used.

stream.description: If `true`, returns a stream of events that happen during the Run as server-sent events, terminating when the Run enters a terminal state with a `data: [DONE]` message.

temperature.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.

tool_resources.description: A set of resources that are used by the assistant's tools. The resources are specific to the type of tool. For example, the `code_interpreter` tool requires a list of file IDs, while the `file_search` tool requires a list of vector store IDs.

tools.description: Override the tools the assistant can use for this run. This is useful for modifying the behavior on a per-run basis.

top_p.description:
An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.

CreateThreadRequest2.title: CreateThreadRequest2
CreateThreadRequest2.description:
Options to create a new thread. If no thread is provided when running a
request, an empty thread will be created.

messages.description: A list of [messages](/docs/api-reference/messages) to start the thread with.

file.description: The audio file object (not file name) to transcribe, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm.

include.description:
Additional information to include in the transcription response.
`logprobs` will return the log probabilities of the tokens in the
response to understand the model's confidence in the transcription.
`logprobs` only works with response_format set to `json` and only with
the models `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`. This field is not supported when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.

keywords.description: Words or phrases to guide transcription of the input audio. Supported by `gpt-transcribe`.

known_speaker_names.description: Optional list of speaker names that correspond to the audio samples provided in `known_speaker_references[]`. Each entry should be a short identifier (for example `customer` or `agent`). Up to 4 speakers are supported.

known_speaker_references.description: Optional list of audio samples (as [data URLs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/Data_URLs)) that contain known speaker references matching `known_speaker_names[]`. Each sample must be between 2 and 10 seconds, and can use any of the same input audio formats supported by `file`.

language.description: The language of the input audio. Supplying the input language in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) (e.g. `en`) format will improve accuracy and latency.

languages.description: Possible languages of the input audio, in [ISO-639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) format. Supported by `gpt-transcribe`.

model.description: ID of the model to use. The options are `gpt-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15`, `whisper-1` (which is powered by our open source Whisper V2 model), and `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.

prompt.description: An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The [prompt](/docs/guides/speech-to-text#prompting) should match the audio language. This field is not supported when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use [log probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability) to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.

timestamp_granularities.description:
The timestamp granularities to populate for this transcription. `response_format` must be set `verbose_json` to use timestamp granularities. Either or both of these options are supported: `word`, or `segment`. Note: There is no additional latency for segment timestamps, but generating word timestamps incurs additional latency.
This option is not available for `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.

CreateTranscriptionResponseDiarizedJson.title: CreateTranscriptionResponseDiarizedJson
CreateTranscriptionResponseDiarizedJson.description: Represents a diarized transcription response returned by the model, including the combined transcript and speaker-segment annotations.

duration.description: Duration of the input audio in seconds.

segments.description: Segments of the transcript annotated with timestamps and speaker labels.

task.description: The type of task that was run. Always `transcribe`.

text.description: The concatenated transcript text for the entire audio input.

usage.description: Token or duration usage statistics for the request.

TranscriptionDiarizedSegment.title: TranscriptionDiarizedSegment
TranscriptionDiarizedSegment.description: A segment of diarized transcript text with speaker metadata.

end.description: End timestamp of the segment in seconds.

id.description: Unique identifier for the segment.

speaker.description: Speaker label for this segment. When known speakers are provided, the label matches `known_speaker_names[]`. Otherwise speakers are labeled sequentially using capital letters (`A`, `B`, ...).

start.description: Start timestamp of the segment in seconds.

text.description: Transcript text for this segment.

type.description: The type of the segment. Always `transcript.text.segment`.

CreateTranscriptionResponseJson.title: CreateTranscriptionResponseJson
CreateTranscriptionResponseJson.description: Represents a transcription response returned by model, based on the provided input.

languages.description: The languages detected in the audio. Returned by `gpt-transcribe`. An empty array indicates that no language could be reliably detected.

logprobs.description: The log probabilities of the tokens in the transcription. Only returned with the models `gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` if `logprobs` is added to the `include` array.

text.description: The transcribed text.

usage.description: Token usage statistics for the request.

TranscriptionLanguage.title: TranscriptionLanguage
TranscriptionLanguage.description: A language detected in transcribed audio.

code.description: The code of a language detected in the audio.

TranscriptTextDeltaEvent.title: TranscriptTextDeltaEvent
TranscriptTextDeltaEvent.description: Emitted when there is an additional text delta. This is also the first event emitted when the transcription starts. Only emitted when you [create a transcription](/docs/api-reference/audio/create-transcription) with the `Stream` parameter set to `true`.

delta.description: The text delta that was additionally transcribed.

logprobs.description: The log probabilities of the delta. Only included if you [create a transcription](/docs/api-reference/audio/create-transcription) with the `include[]` parameter set to `logprobs`.

segment_id.description: Identifier of the diarized segment that this delta belongs to. Only present when using `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`.

type.description: The type of the event. Always `transcript.text.delta`.

TranscriptTextDoneEvent.title: TranscriptTextDoneEvent
TranscriptTextDoneEvent.description: Emitted when the transcription is complete. Contains the complete transcription text. Only emitted when you [create a transcription](/docs/api-reference/audio/create-transcription) with the `Stream` parameter set to `true`.

languages.description: The languages detected in the audio. Returned by `gpt-transcribe`. An empty array indicates that no language could be reliably detected.

logprobs.description: The log probabilities of the individual tokens in the transcription. Only included if you [create a transcription](/docs/api-reference/audio/create-transcription) with the `include[]` parameter set to `logprobs`.

text.description: The text that was transcribed.

type.description: The type of the event. Always `transcript.text.done`.

TranscriptTextSegmentEvent.title: TranscriptTextSegmentEvent
TranscriptTextSegmentEvent.description: Emitted when a diarized transcription returns a completed segment with speaker information. Only emitted when you [create a transcription](/docs/api-reference/audio/create-transcription) with `stream` set to `true` and `response_format` set to `diarized_json`.

end.description: End timestamp of the segment in seconds.

id.description: Unique identifier for the segment.

start.description: Start timestamp of the segment in seconds.

text.description: Transcript text for this segment.

type.description: The type of the event. Always `transcript.text.segment`.

TranscriptTextUsageTokens.title: TranscriptTextUsageTokens
TranscriptTextUsageTokens.description: Usage statistics for models billed by token usage.

input_token_details.description: Details about the input tokens billed for this request.

input_tokens.description: Number of input tokens billed for this request.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used (input + output).

type.description: The type of the usage object. Always `tokens` for this variant.

CreateTranscriptionResponseVerboseJson.title: CreateTranscriptionResponseVerboseJson
CreateTranscriptionResponseVerboseJson.description: Represents a verbose json transcription response returned by model, based on the provided input.

duration.description: The duration of the input audio.

language.description: The language of the input audio.

segments.description: Segments of the transcribed text and their corresponding details.

text.description: The transcribed text.

words.description: Extracted words and their corresponding timestamps.

TranscriptTextUsageDuration.title: TranscriptTextUsageDuration
TranscriptTextUsageDuration.description: Usage statistics for models billed by audio input duration.

seconds.description: Duration of the input audio in seconds.

type.description: The type of the usage object. Always `duration` for this variant.

avg_logprob.description: Average logprob of the segment. If the value is lower than -1, consider the logprobs failed.

compression_ratio.description: Compression ratio of the segment. If the value is greater than 2.4, consider the compression failed.

end.description: End time of the segment in seconds.

id.description: Unique identifier of the segment.

no_speech_prob.description: Probability of no speech in the segment. If the value is higher than 1.0 and the `avg_logprob` is below -1, consider this segment silent.

start.description: Start time of the segment in seconds.

temperature.description: Temperature parameter used for generating the segment.

text.description: Text content of the segment.

tokens.description: Array of token IDs for the text content.

end.description: End time of the word in seconds.

start.description: Start time of the word in seconds.

word.description: The text content of the word.

file.description: The audio file object (not file name) translate, in one of these formats: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm.

model.description: ID of the model to use. Only `whisper-1` (which is powered by our open source Whisper V2 model) is currently available.

prompt.description: An optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment. The [prompt](/docs/guides/speech-to-text#prompting) should be in English.

response_format.description: The format of the output, in one of these options: `json`, `text`, `srt`, `verbose_json`, or `vtt`.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature, between 0 and 1. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. If set to 0, the model will use [log probability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_probability) to automatically increase the temperature until certain thresholds are hit.

duration.description: The duration of the input audio.

language.description: The language of the output translation (always `english`).

segments.description: Segments of the translated text and their corresponding details.

text.description: The translated text.

bytes.description: The number of bytes in the file you are uploading.

filename.description: The name of the file to upload.

mime_type.description:
The MIME type of the file.


This must fall within the supported MIME types for your file purpose. See
the supported MIME types for assistants and vision.

purpose.description:
The intended purpose of the uploaded file.

See the [documentation on File
purposes](/docs/api-reference/files/create#files-create-purpose).

file_ids.description: A list of [File](/docs/api-reference/files) IDs that the vector store should use. Useful for tools like `file_search` that can access files.  If `attributes` or `chunking_strategy` are provided, they will be  applied to all files in the batch. The maximum batch size is 2000 files. This endpoint is recommended for multi-file ingestion and helps reduce per-vector-store write request pressure. Mutually exclusive with `files`.

files.description: A list of objects that each include a `file_id` plus optional `attributes` or `chunking_strategy`. Use this when you need to override metadata for specific files. The global `attributes` or `chunking_strategy` will be ignored and must be specified for each file. The maximum batch size is 2000 files. This endpoint is recommended for multi-file ingestion and helps reduce per-vector-store write request pressure. Mutually exclusive with `file_ids`.

file_id.description: A [File](/docs/api-reference/files) ID that the vector store should use. Useful for tools like `file_search` that can access files. For multi-file ingestion, we recommend [`file_batches`](/docs/api-reference/vector-stores-file-batches/createBatch) to minimize per-vector-store write requests.

chunking_strategy.description: The chunking strategy used to chunk the file(s). If not set, will use the `auto` strategy. Only applicable if `file_ids` is non-empty.

description.description: A description for the vector store. Can be used to describe the vector store's purpose.

file_ids.description: A list of [File](/docs/api-reference/files) IDs that the vector store should use. Useful for tools like `file_search` that can access files.

name.description: The name of the vector store.

VectorStoreExpirationAfter.title: VectorStoreExpirationAfter
VectorStoreExpirationAfter.description: The expiration policy for a vector store.

anchor.description: Anchor timestamp after which the expiration policy applies. Supported anchors: `last_active_at`.

days.description: The number of days after the anchor time that the vector store will expire.

language.description: The BCP 47 language tag for the consent phrase (for example, `en-US`).

name.description: The label to use for this consent recording.

recording.description:
The consent audio recording file. Maximum size is 10 MiB.

Supported MIME types:
`audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/aac`, `audio/flac`, `audio/webm`, `audio/mp4`.

audio_sample.description:
The sample audio recording file. Maximum size is 10 MiB.

Supported MIME types:
`audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/aac`, `audio/flac`, `audio/webm`, `audio/mp4`.

name.description: The name of the new voice.

CustomToolCallOutputResource.title: CustomToolCallOutputResource
CustomToolCallOutputResource.description: The output of a custom tool call from your code, being sent back to the model.

call_id.description: The call ID, used to map this custom tool call output to a custom tool call.

id.description: The unique ID of the custom tool call output in the OpenAI platform.

output.description:
The output from the custom tool call generated by your code.
Can be a string or an list of output content.

type.description: The type of the custom tool call output. Always `custom_tool_call_output`.

CustomToolCallResource.title: CustomToolCallResource
CustomToolCallResource.description: A call to a custom tool created by the model.

call_id.description: An identifier used to map this custom tool call to a tool call output.

id.description: The unique ID of the custom tool call in the OpenAI platform.

input.description: The input for the custom tool call generated by the model.

name.description: The name of the custom tool being called.

namespace.description: The namespace of the custom tool being called.

type.description: The type of the custom tool call. Always `custom_tool_call`.

CustomToolChatCompletions.title: CustomToolChatCompletions
CustomToolChatCompletions.description: A custom tool that processes input using a specified format.

type.description: The type of the custom tool. Always `custom`.

id.description: The ID of the certificate that was deleted.

object.description: The object type, must be `certificate.deleted`.

deleted.description: Whether the fine-tuned model checkpoint permission was successfully deleted.

id.description: The ID of the fine-tuned model checkpoint permission that was deleted.

object.description: The object type, which is always "checkpoint.permission".

DeletedRoleAssignmentResource.title: DeletedRoleAssignmentResource
DeletedRoleAssignmentResource.description: Confirmation payload returned after unassigning a role.

object.description: Identifier for the deleted assignment, such as `group.role.deleted` or `user.role.deleted`.

EasyInputMessage.title: EasyInputMessage
EasyInputMessage.description:
A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take
precedence over instructions given with the `user` role. Messages with the
`assistant` role are presumed to have been generated by the model in previous
interactions.

content.description:
Text, image, or audio input to the model, used to generate a response.
Can also contain previous assistant responses.

role.description:
The role of the message input. One of `user`, `assistant`, `system`, or
`developer`.

type.description: The type of the message input. Always `message`.

EditImageBodyJsonParam.title: EditImageBodyJsonParam
EditImageBodyJsonParam.description:
JSON request body for image edits.

Use `images` (array of `ImageRefParam`) instead of multipart `image` uploads.
You can reference images via external URLs, data URLs, or uploaded file IDs.
JSON edits support GPT image models only; DALL-E edits require multipart (`dall-e-2` only).

background.description: Background behavior for generated image output.

images.description:
Input image references to edit.
For GPT image models, you can provide up to 16 images.

input_fidelity.description: Controls fidelity to the original input image(s).

model.description: The model to use for image editing.

moderation.description: Moderation level for GPT image models.

n.description: The number of edited images to generate.

output_format.description: Output image format. Supported for GPT image models.

prompt.description: A text description of the desired image edit.

quality.description: Output quality for GPT image models.

stream.description: Stream partial image results as events.

user.description:
A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI
monitor and detect abuse.

ImageRefParam.title: ImageRefParam
ImageRefParam.description:
Reference an input image by either URL or uploaded file ID.
Provide exactly one of `image_url` or `file_id`.

file_id.description: The File API ID of an uploaded image to use as input.

image_url.description: A fully qualified URL or base64-encoded data URL.

Eval.title: Eval
Eval.description:
An Eval object with a data source config and testing criteria.
An Eval represents a task to be done for your LLM integration.
Like:
 - Improve the quality of my chatbot
 - See how well my chatbot handles customer support
 - Check if o4-mini is better at my usecase than gpt-4o

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the eval was created.

data_source_config.description: Configuration of data sources used in runs of the evaluation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the evaluation.

name.description: The name of the evaluation.

object.description: The object type.

EvalApiError.title: EvalApiError
EvalApiError.description: An object representing an error response from the Eval API.

EvalCustomDataSourceConfig.title: EvalCustomDataSourceConfig
EvalCustomDataSourceConfig.description:
A CustomDataSourceConfig which specifies the schema of your `item` and optionally `sample` namespaces.
The response schema defines the shape of the data that will be:
- Used to define your testing criteria and
- What data is required when creating a run

schema.description:
The json schema for the run data source items.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

type.description: The type of data source. Always `custom`.

EvalItem.title: EvalItem
EvalItem.description:
A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take
precedence over instructions given with the `user` role. Messages with the
`assistant` role are presumed to have been generated by the model in previous
interactions.

role.description:
The role of the message input. One of `user`, `assistant`, `system`, or
`developer`.

type.description: The type of the message input. Always `message`.

EvalItemContent.title: EvalItemContent
EvalItemContent.description: Inputs to the model - can contain template strings. Supports text, output text, input images, and input audio, either as a single item or an array of items.

EvalItemContentItem.title: EvalItemContentItem
EvalItemContentItem.description: A single content item: input text, output text, input image, or input audio.

EvalItemContentOutputText.title: EvalItemContentOutputText
EvalItemContentOutputText.description: A text output from the model.

text.description: The text output from the model.

type.description: The type of the output text. Always `output_text`.

EvalItemInputImage.title: EvalItemInputImage
EvalItemInputImage.description: An image input block used within EvalItem content arrays.

detail.description: The detail level of the image to be sent to the model. One of `high`, `low`, or `auto`. Defaults to `auto`.

image_url.description: The URL of the image input.

type.description: The type of the image input. Always `input_image`.

InputAudio.title: InputAudio
InputAudio.description: An audio input to the model.

type.description: The type of the input item. Always `input_audio`.

content.description: The content of the jsonl file.

type.description: The type of jsonl source. Always `file_content`.

id.description: The identifier of the file.

type.description: The type of jsonl source. Always `file_id`.

EvalList.title: EvalList
EvalList.description: An object representing a list of evals.

first_id.description: The identifier of the first eval in the data array.

has_more.description: Indicates whether there are more evals available.

last_id.description: The identifier of the last eval in the data array.

object.description: The type of this object. It is always set to "list".

EvalLogsDataSourceConfig.title: EvalLogsDataSourceConfig
EvalLogsDataSourceConfig.description:
A LogsDataSourceConfig which specifies the metadata property of your logs query.
This is usually metadata like `usecase=chatbot` or `prompt-version=v2`, etc.
The schema returned by this data source config is used to defined what variables are available in your evals.
`item` and `sample` are both defined when using this data source config.

schema.description:
The json schema for the run data source items.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

type.description: The type of data source. Always `logs`.

EvalResponsesSource.title: EvalResponsesSource
EvalResponsesSource.description: A EvalResponsesSource object describing a run data source configuration.

type.description: The type of run data source. Always `responses`.

EvalRun.title: EvalRun
EvalRun.description: A schema representing an evaluation run.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the evaluation run was created.

data_source.description: Information about the run's data source.

eval_id.description: The identifier of the associated evaluation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the evaluation run.

model.description: The model that is evaluated, if applicable.

name.description: The name of the evaluation run.

object.description: The type of the object. Always "eval.run".

per_model_usage.description: Usage statistics for each model during the evaluation run.

per_testing_criteria_results.description: Results per testing criteria applied during the evaluation run.

report_url.description: The URL to the rendered evaluation run report on the UI dashboard.

result_counts.description: Counters summarizing the outcomes of the evaluation run.

status.description: The status of the evaluation run.

EvalRunList.title: EvalRunList
EvalRunList.description: An object representing a list of runs for an evaluation.

data.description: An array of eval run objects.

first_id.description: The identifier of the first eval run in the data array.

has_more.description: Indicates whether there are more evals available.

last_id.description: The identifier of the last eval run in the data array.

object.description: The type of this object. It is always set to "list".

EvalRunOutputItem.title: EvalRunOutputItem
EvalRunOutputItem.description: A schema representing an evaluation run output item.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the evaluation run was created.

datasource_item.description: Details of the input data source item.

datasource_item_id.description: The identifier for the data source item.

eval_id.description: The identifier of the evaluation group.

id.description: Unique identifier for the evaluation run output item.

object.description: The type of the object. Always "eval.run.output_item".

results.description: A list of grader results for this output item.

run_id.description: The identifier of the evaluation run associated with this output item.

sample.description: A sample containing the input and output of the evaluation run.

status.description: The status of the evaluation run.

EvalRunOutputItemResult.title: EvalRunOutputItemResult
EvalRunOutputItemResult.description: A single grader result for an evaluation run output item.

name.description: The name of the grader.

passed.description: Whether the grader considered the output a pass.

sample.description: Optional sample or intermediate data produced by the grader.

score.description: The numeric score produced by the grader.

type.description: The grader type (for example, "string-check-grader").

EvalRunOutputItemList.title: EvalRunOutputItemList
EvalRunOutputItemList.description: An object representing a list of output items for an evaluation run.

data.description: An array of eval run output item objects.

first_id.description: The identifier of the first eval run output item in the data array.

has_more.description: Indicates whether there are more eval run output items available.

last_id.description: The identifier of the last eval run output item in the data array.

object.description: The type of this object. It is always set to "list".

schema.description:
The json schema for the run data source items.
Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/).

type.description: The type of data source. Always `stored_completions`.

EvalStoredCompletionsSource.title: EvalStoredCompletionsSource
EvalStoredCompletionsSource.description: A StoredCompletionsRunDataSource configuration describing a set of filters

type.description: The type of source. Always `stored_completions`.

FileSearchRanker.title: FileSearchRanker
FileSearchRanker.description: The ranker to use for the file search. If not specified will use the `auto` ranker.

FileSearchRankingOptions.title: FileSearchRankingOptions
FileSearchRankingOptions.description:
The ranking options for the file search. If not specified, the file search tool will use the `auto` ranker and a score_threshold of 0.

See the [file search tool documentation](/docs/assistants/tools/file-search#customizing-file-search-settings) for more information.

score_threshold.description: The score threshold for the file search. All values must be a floating point number between 0 and 1.

FineTuningCheckpointPermission.title: FineTuningCheckpointPermission
FineTuningCheckpointPermission.description: The `checkpoint.permission` object represents a permission for a fine-tuned model checkpoint.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the permission was created.

id.description: The permission identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always "checkpoint.permission".

project_id.description: The project identifier that the permission is for.

type.description: The type of the integration being enabled for the fine-tuning job

wandb.description:
The settings for your integration with Weights and Biases. This payload specifies the project that
metrics will be sent to. Optionally, you can set an explicit display name for your run, add tags
to your run, and set a default entity (team, username, etc) to be associated with your run.

FineTuningJob.title: FineTuningJob
FineTuningJob.description: The `fine_tuning.job` object represents a fine-tuning job that has been created through the API.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the fine-tuning job was created.

hyperparameters.description: The hyperparameters used for the fine-tuning job. This value will only be returned when running `supervised` jobs.

id.description: The object identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.

model.description: The base model that is being fine-tuned.

object.description: The object type, which is always "fine_tuning.job".

organization_id.description: The organization that owns the fine-tuning job.

result_files.description: The compiled results file ID(s) for the fine-tuning job. You can retrieve the results with the [Files API](/docs/api-reference/files/retrieve-contents).

seed.description: The seed used for the fine-tuning job.

status.description: The current status of the fine-tuning job, which can be either `validating_files`, `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

training_file.description: The file ID used for training. You can retrieve the training data with the [Files API](/docs/api-reference/files/retrieve-contents).

FineTuningJobCheckpoint.title: FineTuningJobCheckpoint
FineTuningJobCheckpoint.description: The `fine_tuning.job.checkpoint` object represents a model checkpoint for a fine-tuning job that is ready to use.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the checkpoint was created.

fine_tuned_model_checkpoint.description: The name of the fine-tuned checkpoint model that is created.

fine_tuning_job_id.description: The name of the fine-tuning job that this checkpoint was created from.

id.description: The checkpoint identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.

metrics.description: Metrics at the step number during the fine-tuning job.

object.description: The object type, which is always "fine_tuning.job.checkpoint".

step_number.description: The step number that the checkpoint was created at.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the fine-tuning job was created.

data.description: The data associated with the event.

id.description: The object identifier.

level.description: The log level of the event.

object.description: The object type, which is always "fine_tuning.job.event".

type.description: The type of event.

FunctionToolCall.title: FunctionToolCall
FunctionToolCall.description:
A tool call to run a function. See the
[function calling guide](/docs/guides/function-calling) for more information.

arguments.description: A JSON string of the arguments to pass to the function.

call_id.description: The unique ID of the function tool call generated by the model.

id.description: The unique ID of the function tool call.

name.description: The name of the function to run.

namespace.description: The namespace of the function to run.

status.description:
The status of the item. One of `in_progress`, `completed`, or
`incomplete`. Populated when items are returned via API.

type.description: The type of the function tool call. Always `function_call`.

FunctionToolCallOutput.title: FunctionToolCallOutput
FunctionToolCallOutput.description: The output of a function tool call.

call_id.description: The unique ID of the function tool call generated by the model.

id.description:
The unique ID of the function tool call output. Populated when this item
is returned via API.

name.description: The name of the tool that produced the output.

namespace.description: The namespace of the tool that produced the output.

output.description:
The output from the function call generated by your code.
Can be a string or an list of output content.

status.description:
The status of the item. One of `in_progress`, `completed`, or
`incomplete`. Populated when items are returned via API.

type.description: The type of the function tool call output. Always `function_call_output`.

GraderLabelModel.title: GraderLabelModel
GraderLabelModel.description:
A LabelModelGrader object which uses a model to assign labels to each item
in the evaluation.

labels.description: The labels to assign to each item in the evaluation.

model.description: The model to use for the evaluation. Must support structured outputs.

name.description: The name of the grader.

passing_labels.description: The labels that indicate a passing result. Must be a subset of labels.

type.description: The object type, which is always `label_model`.

GraderMulti.title: GraderMulti
GraderMulti.description: A MultiGrader object combines the output of multiple graders to produce a single score.

calculate_output.description: A formula to calculate the output based on grader results.

name.description: The name of the grader.

type.description: The object type, which is always `multi`.

GraderPython.title: GraderPython
GraderPython.description: A PythonGrader object that runs a python script on the input.

image_tag.description: The image tag to use for the python script.

name.description: The name of the grader.

source.description: The source code of the python script.

type.description: The object type, which is always `python`.

GraderScoreModel.title: GraderScoreModel
GraderScoreModel.description: A ScoreModelGrader object that uses a model to assign a score to the input.

input.description: The input messages evaluated by the grader. Supports text, output text, input image, and input audio content blocks, and may include template strings.

model.description: The model to use for the evaluation.

name.description: The name of the grader.

range.description: The range of the score. Defaults to `[0, 1]`.

sampling_params.description: The sampling parameters for the model.

type.description: The object type, which is always `score_model`.

GraderStringCheck.title: GraderStringCheck
GraderStringCheck.description: A StringCheckGrader object that performs a string comparison between input and reference using a specified operation.

input.description: The input text. This may include template strings.

name.description: The name of the grader.

operation.description: The string check operation to perform. One of `eq`, `ne`, `like`, or `ilike`.

reference.description: The reference text. This may include template strings.

type.description: The object type, which is always `string_check`.

GraderTextSimilarity.title: GraderTextSimilarity
GraderTextSimilarity.description: A TextSimilarityGrader object which grades text based on similarity metrics.

evaluation_metric.description:
The evaluation metric to use. One of `cosine`, `fuzzy_match`, `bleu`,
`gleu`, `meteor`, `rouge_1`, `rouge_2`, `rouge_3`, `rouge_4`, `rouge_5`,
or `rouge_l`.

input.description: The text being graded.

name.description: The name of the grader.

type.description: The type of grader.

Group.title: Group
Group.description: Summary information about a group returned in role assignment responses.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the group was created.

id.description: Identifier for the group.

name.description: Display name of the group.

object.description: Always `group`.

scim_managed.description: Whether the group is managed through SCIM.

GroupDeletedResource.title: GroupDeletedResource
GroupDeletedResource.description: Confirmation payload returned after deleting a group.

id.description: Identifier of the deleted group.

object.description: Always `group.deleted`.

data.description: Groups returned in the current page.

has_more.description: Whether additional groups are available when paginating.

next.description: Cursor to fetch the next page of results, or `null` if there are no more results.

object.description: Always `list`.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the group was created.

id.description: Identifier for the group.

is_scim_managed.description: Whether the group is managed through SCIM and controlled by your identity provider.

name.description: Display name of the group.

GroupMemberUser.title: GroupMemberUser

HostedToolPermission.title: HostedToolPermission
HostedToolPermission.description: Permission state for a single hosted tool on a project.

Image.title: Image
Image.description: Represents the content or the URL of an image generated by the OpenAI API.

b64_json.description: The base64-encoded JSON of the generated image. Returned by default for the GPT image models, and only present if `response_format` is set to `b64_json` for `dall-e-2` and `dall-e-3`.

ImageEditCompletedEvent.title: ImageEditCompletedEvent
ImageEditCompletedEvent.description: Emitted when image editing has completed and the final image is available.

b64_json.description: Base64-encoded final edited image data, suitable for rendering as an image.

background.description: The background setting for the edited image.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp when the event was created.

output_format.description: The output format for the edited image.

quality.description: The quality setting for the edited image.

size.description: The size of the edited image.

ImagesUsage.title: ImagesUsage
ImagesUsage.description: For the GPT image models only, the token usage information for the image generation.

ImageEditPartialImageEvent.title: ImageEditPartialImageEvent
ImageEditPartialImageEvent.description: Emitted when a partial image is available during image editing streaming.

output_format.description: The output format for the requested edited image.

quality.description: The quality setting for the requested edited image.

ImageGenCompletedEvent.title: ImageGenCompletedEvent
ImageGenCompletedEvent.description: Emitted when image generation has completed and the final image is available.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp when the event was created.

output_format.description: The output format for the generated image.

quality.description: The quality setting for the generated image.

size.description: The size of the generated image.

ImageGenPartialImageEvent.title: ImageGenPartialImageEvent
ImageGenPartialImageEvent.description: Emitted when a partial image is available during image generation streaming.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp when the event was created.

output_format.description: The output format for the requested image.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the image was created.

output_format.description: The output format of the image generation. Either `png`, `webp`, or `jpeg`.

quality.description: The quality of the image generated. Either `low`, `medium`, or `high`.

size.description: The size of the image generated. Either `1024x1024`, `1024x1536`, or `1536x1024`.

ImageGenInputUsageDetails.title: ImageGenInputUsageDetails

InputMessage.title: InputMessage
InputMessage.description:
A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take
precedence over instructions given with the `user` role.

status.description:
The status of item. One of `in_progress`, `completed`, or
`incomplete`. Populated when items are returned via API.

InputMessageResource.title: InputMessageResource
InputMessageResource.description:
A message input to the model with a role indicating instruction following
hierarchy. Instructions given with the `developer` or `system` role take

status.description:
The status of item. One of `in_progress`, `completed`, or

type.description: The type of the message input. Always set to `message`.

Invite.title: Invite
Invite.description: Represents an individual `invite` to the organization.

accepted_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the invite was accepted.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the invite was sent.

email.description: The email address of the individual to whom the invite was sent

expires_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the invite expires.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints

object.description: The object type, which is always `organization.invite`

projects.description: The projects that were granted membership upon acceptance of the invite.

status.description: `accepted`,`expired`, or `pending`

object.description: The object type, which is always `organization.invite.deleted`

has_more.description: The `has_more` property is used for pagination to indicate there are additional results.

InviteProjectGroupBody.title: InviteProjectGroupBody
InviteProjectGroupBody.description: Request payload for granting a group access to a project.

If omitted, the user will be invited to the default project for compatibility with legacy behavior. If empty list is passed, the user will not be invited to any projects, including the default one.

ItemResource.title: ItemResource
ItemResource.description: Content item used to generate a response.

OutputMessage.title: OutputMessage
OutputMessage.description: An output message from the model.

OrganizationCertificate.title: OrganizationCertificate
OrganizationCertificate.description: Represents an individual certificate configured at the organization level.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints

name.description: The name of the certificate.

OpenAIFile.title: OpenAIFile
OpenAIFile.description: The `File` object represents a document that has been uploaded to OpenAI.

bytes.description: The size of the file, in bytes.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the file was created.

expires_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the file will expire.

id.description: The file identifier, which can be referenced in the API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always `file`.

purpose.description: The intended purpose of the file. Supported values are `assistants`, `assistants_output`, `batch`, `batch_output`, `fine-tune`, `fine-tune-results`, `vision`, and `user_data`.

status.description: Deprecated. The current status of the file, which can be either `uploaded`, `processed`, or `error`.

status_details.description: Deprecated. For details on why a fine-tuning training file failed validation, see the `error` field on `fine_tuning.job`.

content.description: The content of the message in array of text and/or images.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the message was created.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always `thread.message`.

role.description: The entity that produced the message. One of `user` or `assistant`.

status.description: The status of the message, which can be either `in_progress`, `incomplete`, or `completed`.

thread_id.description: The [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads) ID that this message belongs to.

Model.title: Model
Model.description: Describes an OpenAI model offering that can be used with the API.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) when the model was created.

object.description: The object type, which is always "model".

OrganizationProjectCertificate.title: OrganizationProjectCertificate
OrganizationProjectCertificate.description: Represents an individual certificate configured at the project level.

name.description: The name of the certificate.

RunStepObject.title: RunStepObject
RunStepObject.description: Represents a step in execution of a run.

assistant_id.description: The ID of the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) associated with the run step.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run step was created.

id.description: The identifier of the run step, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

object.description: The object type, which is always `thread.run.step`.

run_id.description: The ID of the [run](/docs/api-reference/runs) that this run step is a part of.

status.description: The status of the run step, which can be either `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `completed`, or `expired`.

step_details.description: The details of the run step.

thread_id.description: The ID of the [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads) that was run.

type.description: The type of run step, which can be either `message_creation` or `tool_calls`.

RunObject.title: RunObject
RunObject.description: Represents an execution run on a [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads).

assistant_id.description: The ID of the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for execution of this run.

cancelled_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was cancelled.

completed_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was completed.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was created.

expires_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run will expire.

failed_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run failed.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

incomplete_details.description: Details on why the run is incomplete. Will be `null` if the run is not incomplete.

instructions.description: The instructions that the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for this run.

last_error.description: The last error associated with this run. Will be `null` if there are no errors.

max_completion_tokens.description: The maximum number of completion tokens specified to have been used over the course of the run.

max_prompt_tokens.description: The maximum number of prompt tokens specified to have been used over the course of the run.

model.description: The model that the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for this run.

object.description: The object type, which is always `thread.run`.

required_action.description: Details on the action required to continue the run. Will be `null` if no action is required.

started_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the run was started.

status.description: The status of the run, which can be either `queued`, `in_progress`, `requires_action`, `cancelling`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `completed`, `incomplete`, or `expired`.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature used for this run. If not set, defaults to 1.

thread_id.description: The ID of the [thread](/docs/api-reference/threads) that was executed on as a part of this run.

tools.description: The list of tools that the [assistant](/docs/api-reference/assistants) used for this run.

top_p.description: The nucleus sampling value used for this run. If not set, defaults to 1.

VectorStoreFileObject.title: VectorStoreFileObject
VectorStoreFileObject.description: A list of files attached to a vector store.

chunking_strategy.description: The strategy used to chunk the file.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the vector store file was created.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

usage_bytes.description: The total vector store usage in bytes. Note that this may be different from the original file size.

VectorStoreObject.description: A vector store is a collection of processed files can be used by the `file_search` tool.

id.description: The identifier, which can be referenced in API endpoints.

name.description: The name of the vector store.

usage_bytes.description: The total number of bytes used by the files in the vector store.

bytes.description: The bytes that were used to generate the log probability.

logprob.description: The log probability of the token.

token.description: The token that was used to generate the log probability.

MCP server is [annotated with `readOnlyHint`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/schema#toolannotations-readonlyhint),

RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemC.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemCreate
RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemC.description:
Add a new Item to the Conversation's context, including messages, function
calls, and function call responses. This event can be used both to populate a
"history" of the conversation and to add new items mid-stream, but has the
current limitation that it cannot populate assistant audio messages.

If successful, the server will respond with a `conversation.item.created`
event, otherwise an `error` event will be sent.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

previous_item_id.description:
The ID of the preceding item after which the new item will be inserted.
If not set, the new item will be appended to the end of the conversation.
If set to `root`, the new item will be added to the beginning of the conversation.
If set to an existing ID, it allows an item to be inserted mid-conversation. If the
ID cannot be found, an error will be returned and the item will not be added.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.create`.

RealtimeConversationItem.title: RealtimeConversationItem

RealtimeConversationItemFunctionCall.description: A function call item in a Realtime conversation.

arguments.description: The arguments of the function call. This is a JSON-encoded string representing the arguments passed to the function, for example `{"arg1": "value1", "arg2": 42}`.

id.description: The unique ID of the item. This may be provided by the client or generated by the server.

name.description: The name of the function being called.

object.description: Identifier for the API object being returned - always `realtime.item`. Optional when creating a new item.

status.description: The status of the item. Has no effect on the conversation.

type.description: The type of the item. Always `function_call`.

RealtimeConversationItemMessageSystem.title: RealtimeConversationItemMessageSystem
RealtimeConversationItemMessageSystem.description: A system message in a Realtime conversation can be used to provide additional context or instructions to the model. This is similar but distinct from the instruction prompt provided at the start of a conversation, as system messages can be added at any point in the conversation. For major changes to the conversation's behavior, use instructions, but for smaller updates (e.g. "the user is now asking about a different topic"), use system messages.

content.description: The content of the message.

id.description: The unique ID of the item. This may be provided by the client or generated by the server.

object.description: Identifier for the API object being returned - always `realtime.item`. Optional when creating a new item.

role.description: The role of the message sender. Always `system`.

status.description: The status of the item. Has no effect on the conversation.

type.description: The type of the item. Always `message`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemD.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemDelete
RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemD.description:
Send this event when you want to remove any item from the conversation
history. The server will respond with a `conversation.item.deleted` event,
unless the item does not exist in the conversation history, in which case the
server will respond with an error.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

item_id.description: The ID of the item to delete.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.delete`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemR.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemRetrieve
RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemR.description:
Send this event when you want to retrieve the server's representation of a specific item in the conversation history. This is useful, for example, to inspect user audio after noise cancellation and VAD.
The server will respond with a `conversation.item.retrieved` event,
unless the item does not exist in the conversation history, in which case the
server will respond with an error.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

item_id.description: The ID of the item to retrieve.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.retrieve`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemT.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemTruncate
RealtimeBetaClientEventConversationItemT.description:
Send this event to truncate a previous assistant message’s audio. The server
will produce audio faster than realtime, so this event is useful when the user
interrupts to truncate audio that has already been sent to the client but not
yet played. This will synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with
the client's playback.

Truncating audio will delete the server-side text transcript to ensure there
is not text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.

If successful, the server will respond with a `conversation.item.truncated`
event.

audio_end_ms.description:
Inclusive duration up to which audio is truncated, in milliseconds. If
the audio_end_ms is greater than the actual audio duration, the server
will respond with an error.

content_index.description: The index of the content part to truncate. Set this to 0.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

item_id.description:
The ID of the assistant message item to truncate. Only assistant message
items can be truncated.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.truncate`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferA.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferAppend
RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferA.description:
Send this event to append audio bytes to the input audio buffer. The audio
buffer is temporary storage you can write to and later commit. In Server VAD
mode, the audio buffer is used to detect speech and the server will decide
when to commit. When Server VAD is disabled, you must commit the audio buffer
manually.

The client may choose how much audio to place in each event up to a maximum
of 15 MiB, for example streaming smaller chunks from the client may allow the
VAD to be more responsive. Unlike made other client events, the server will
not send a confirmation response to this event.

audio.description:
Base64-encoded audio bytes. This must be in the format specified by the
`input_audio_format` field in the session configuration.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

type.description: The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.append`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferC.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferClear
RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferC.description:
Send this event to clear the audio bytes in the buffer. The server will
respond with an `input_audio_buffer.cleared` event.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

type.description: The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.clear`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferC.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferCommit
RealtimeBetaClientEventInputAudioBufferC.description:
Send this event to commit the user input audio buffer, which will create a
new user message item in the conversation. This event will produce an error
if the input audio buffer is empty. When in Server VAD mode, the client does
not need to send this event, the server will commit the audio buffer
automatically.

Committing the input audio buffer will trigger input audio transcription
(if enabled in session configuration), but it will not create a response
from the model. The server will respond with an `input_audio_buffer.committed`
event.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

type.description: The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.commit`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventOutputAudioBuffer.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventOutputAudioBufferClear
RealtimeBetaClientEventOutputAudioBuffer.description:
**WebRTC/SIP Only:** Emit to cut off the current audio response. This will trigger the server to
stop generating audio and emit a `output_audio_buffer.cleared` event. This
event should be preceded by a `response.cancel` client event to stop the
generation of the current response.
[Learn more](/docs/guides/realtime-conversations#client-and-server-events-for-audio-in-webrtc).

event_id.description: The unique ID of the client event used for error handling.

type.description: The event type, must be `output_audio_buffer.clear`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCancel.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCancel
RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCancel.description:
Send this event to cancel an in-progress response. The server will respond
with a `response.done` event with a status of `response.status=cancelled`. If
there is no response to cancel, the server will respond with an error.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

response_id.description:
A specific response ID to cancel - if not provided, will cancel an
in-progress response in the default conversation.

type.description: The event type, must be `response.cancel`.

RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCreate.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCreate
RealtimeBetaClientEventResponseCreate.description:
This event instructs the server to create a Response, which means triggering
model inference. When in Server VAD mode, the server will create Responses
automatically.

A Response will include at least one Item, and may have two, in which case
the second will be a function call. These Items will be appended to the
conversation history.

The server will respond with a `response.created` event, events for Items
and content created, and finally a `response.done` event to indicate the
Response is complete.

The `response.create` event can optionally include inference configuration like
`instructions`, and `temperature`. These fields will override the Session's
configuration for this Response only.

Responses can be created out-of-band of the default Conversation, meaning that they can
have arbitrary input, and it's possible to disable writing the output to the Conversation.
Only one Response can write to the default Conversation at a time, but otherwise multiple
Responses can be created in parallel.

Clients can set `conversation` to `none` to create a Response that does not write to the default
Conversation. Arbitrary input can be provided with the `input` field, which is an array accepting
raw Items and references to existing Items.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

type.description: The event type, must be `response.create`.

RealtimeBetaResponseCreateParams.title: RealtimeBetaResponseCreateParams
RealtimeBetaResponseCreateParams.description: Create a new Realtime response with these parameters

conversation.description:
Controls which conversation the response is added to. Currently supports
`auto` and `none`, with `auto` as the default value. The `auto` value
means that the contents of the response will be added to the default
conversation. Set this to `none` to create an out-of-band response which
will not add items to default conversation.

input.description:
Input items to include in the prompt for the model. Using this field
creates a new context for this Response instead of using the default
conversation. An empty array `[]` will clear the context for this Response.
Note that this can include references to items from the default conversation.

instructions.description:
The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model
calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired
responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format,
(e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good
responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion
into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed
to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the
desired behavior.

Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this
field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the
start of the session.

max_output_tokens.description:
Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,
inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to
limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a
given model. Defaults to `inf`.

modalities.description:
The set of modalities the model can respond with. To disable audio,
set this to ["text"].

output_audio_format.description: The format of output audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature for the model, limited to [0.6, 1.2]. Defaults to 0.8.

tool_choice.description:
How the model chooses tools. Provide one of the string modes or force a specific
function/MCP tool.

tools.description: Tools (functions) available to the model.

RealtimeBetaClientEventSessionUpdate.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventSessionUpdate
RealtimeBetaClientEventSessionUpdate.description:
Send this event to update the session’s default configuration.
The client may send this event at any time to update any field,
except for `voice`. However, note that once a session has been
initialized with a particular `model`, it can’t be changed to
another model using `session.update`.

When the server receives a `session.update`, it will respond
with a `session.updated` event showing the full, effective configuration.
Only the fields that are present are updated. To clear a field like
`instructions`, pass an empty string.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

type.description: The event type, must be `session.update`.

RealtimeSessionCreateRequest.title: RealtimeSessionCreateRequest
RealtimeSessionCreateRequest.description:
A new Realtime session configuration, with an ephemeral key. Default TTL
for keys is one minute.

client_secret.description: Ephemeral key returned by the API.

input_audio_format.description: The format of input audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.

input_audio_transcription.description:
Configuration for input audio transcription, defaults to off and can be
set to `null` to turn off once on. Input audio transcription is not native
to the model, since the model consumes audio directly. Transcription runs
asynchronously and should be treated as rough guidance
rather than the representation understood by the model.

instructions.description:
The default system instructions (i.e. system message) prepended to model calls. This field allows the client to guide the model on desired responses. The model can be instructed on response content and format, (e.g. "be extremely succinct", "act friendly", "here are examples of good responses") and on audio behavior (e.g. "talk quickly", "inject emotion into your voice", "laugh frequently"). The instructions are not guaranteed to be followed by the model, but they provide guidance to the model on the desired behavior.
Note that the server sets default instructions which will be used if this field is not set and are visible in the `session.created` event at the start of the session.

max_response_output_tokens.description:
Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,
inclusive of tool calls. Provide an integer between 1 and 4096 to
limit output tokens, or `inf` for the maximum available tokens for a
given model. Defaults to `inf`.

modalities.description:
The set of modalities the model can respond with. To disable audio,
set this to ["text"].

output_audio_format.description: The format of output audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.

speed.description:
The speed of the model's spoken response. 1.0 is the default speed. 0.25 is
the minimum speed. 1.5 is the maximum speed. This value can only be changed
in between model turns, not while a response is in progress.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature for the model, limited to [0.6, 1.2]. Defaults to 0.8.

tool_choice.description:
How the model chooses tools. Options are `auto`, `none`, `required`, or
specify a function.

tools.description: Tools (functions) available to the model.

tracing.description:
Configuration options for tracing. Set to null to disable tracing. Once
tracing is enabled for a session, the configuration cannot be modified.

`auto` will create a trace for the session with default values for the
workflow name, group id, and metadata.

turn_detection.description:
Configuration for turn detection. Can be set to `null` to turn off. Server
VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on
audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.

RealtimeTruncation.title: RealtimeTruncation
RealtimeTruncation.description:
When the number of tokens in a conversation exceeds the model's input token limit, the conversation be truncated, meaning messages (starting from the oldest) will not be included in the model's context. A 32k context model with 4,096 max output tokens can only include 28,224 tokens in the context before truncation occurs.

Clients can configure truncation behavior to truncate with a lower max token limit, which is an effective way to control token usage and cost.

Truncation will reduce the number of cached tokens on the next turn (busting the cache), since messages are dropped from the beginning of the context. However, clients can also configure truncation to retain messages up to a fraction of the maximum context size, which will reduce the need for future truncations and thus improve the cache rate.

Truncation can be disabled entirely, which means the server will never truncate but would instead return an error if the conversation exceeds the model's input token limit.

RealtimeBetaClientEventTranscriptionSess.title: RealtimeBetaClientEventTranscriptionSessionUpdate
RealtimeBetaClientEventTranscriptionSess.description: Send this event to update a transcription session.

event_id.description: Optional client-generated ID used to identify this event.

type.description: The event type, must be `transcription_session.update`.

include.description:
The set of items to include in the transcription. Current available items are:
`item.input_audio_transcription.logprobs`

input_audio_format.description:
The format of input audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.
For `pcm16`, input audio must be 16-bit PCM at a 24kHz sample rate,
single channel (mono), and little-endian byte order.

input_audio_noise_reduction.description:
Configuration for input audio noise reduction. This can be set to `null` to turn off.
Noise reduction filters audio added to the input audio buffer before it is sent to VAD and the model.
Filtering the audio can improve VAD and turn detection accuracy (reducing false positives) and model performance by improving perception of the input audio.

turn_detection.description: Configuration for turn detection. Can be set to `null` to turn off. Server VAD means that the model will detect the start and end of speech based on audio volume and respond at the end of user speech.

conversation_id.description:
Which conversation the response is added to, determined by the `conversation`
field in the `response.create` event. If `auto`, the response will be added to
the default conversation and the value of `conversation_id` will be an id like
`conv_1234`. If `none`, the response will not be added to any conversation and
the value of `conversation_id` will be `null`. If responses are being triggered
by server VAD, the response will be added to the default conversation, thus
the `conversation_id` will be an id like `conv_1234`.

id.description: The unique ID of the response.

max_output_tokens.description:
Maximum number of output tokens for a single assistant response,
inclusive of tool calls, that was used in this response.

modalities.description:
The set of modalities the model used to respond. If there are multiple modalities,
the model will pick one, for example if `modalities` is `["text", "audio"]`, the model
could be responding in either text or audio.

object.description: The object type, must be `realtime.response`.

output.description: The list of output items generated by the response.

output_audio_format.description: The format of output audio. Options are `pcm16`, `g711_ulaw`, or `g711_alaw`.

status.description:
The final status of the response (`completed`, `cancelled`, `failed`, or
`incomplete`, `in_progress`).

temperature.description: Sampling temperature for the model, limited to [0.6, 1.2]. Defaults to 0.8.

usage.description:
Usage statistics for the Response, this will correspond to billing. A
Realtime API session will maintain a conversation context and append new
Items to the Conversation, thus output from previous turns (text and
audio tokens) will become the input for later turns.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemC.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemCreated
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemC.description:
Returned when a conversation item is created. There are several scenarios that produce this event:
  - The server is generating a Response, which if successful will produce
    either one or two Items, which will be of type `message`
    (role `assistant`) or type `function_call`.
  - The input audio buffer has been committed, either by the client or the
    server (in `server_vad` mode). The server will take the content of the
    input audio buffer and add it to a new user message Item.
  - The client has sent a `conversation.item.create` event to add a new Item
    to the Conversation.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.created`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemD.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemDeleted
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemD.description:
Returned when an item in the conversation is deleted by the client with a
`conversation.item.delete` event. This event is used to synchronize the
server's understanding of the conversation history with the client's view.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

item_id.description: The ID of the item that was deleted.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.deleted`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionCompleted
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.description:
This event is the output of audio transcription for user audio written to the
user audio buffer. Transcription begins when the input audio buffer is
committed by the client or server (in `server_vad` mode). Transcription runs
asynchronously with Response creation, so this event may come before or after
the Response events.

Realtime API models accept audio natively, and thus input transcription is a
separate process run on a separate ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) model.
The transcript may diverge somewhat from the model's interpretation, and
should be treated as a rough guide.

content_index.description: The index of the content part containing the audio.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

item_id.description: The ID of the user message item containing the audio.

languages.description: The languages detected in the audio. Returned by `gpt-transcribe`. An empty array indicates that no language could be reliably detected.

type.description:
The event type, must be
`conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionDelta
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.description: Returned when the text value of an input audio transcription content part is updated.

content_index.description: The index of the content part in the item's content array.

delta.description: The text delta.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

item_id.description: The ID of the item.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionFailed
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.description:
Returned when input audio transcription is configured, and a transcription
request for a user message failed. These events are separate from other
`error` events so that the client can identify the related Item.

content_index.description: The index of the content part containing the audio.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

item_id.description: The ID of the user message item.

type.description:
The event type, must be
`conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.failed`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemInputAudioTranscriptionSegment
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemI.description: Returned when an input audio transcription segment is identified for an item.

content_index.description: The index of the input audio content part within the item.

end.description: End time of the segment in seconds.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

id.description: The segment identifier.

item_id.description: The ID of the item containing the input audio content.

speaker.description: The detected speaker label for this segment.

start.description: Start time of the segment in seconds.

text.description: The text for this segment.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.segment`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemR.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemRetrieved
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemR.description: Returned when a conversation item is retrieved with `conversation.item.retrieve`.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.retrieved`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemT.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemTruncated
RealtimeBetaServerEventConversationItemT.description:
Returned when an earlier assistant audio message item is truncated by the
client with a `conversation.item.truncate` event. This event is used to
synchronize the server's understanding of the audio with the client's playback.

This action will truncate the audio and remove the server-side text transcript
to ensure there is no text in the context that hasn't been heard by the user.

audio_end_ms.description: The duration up to which the audio was truncated, in milliseconds.

content_index.description: The index of the content part that was truncated.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

item_id.description: The ID of the assistant message item that was truncated.

type.description: The event type, must be `conversation.item.truncated`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventError.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventError
RealtimeBetaServerEventError.description:
Returned when an error occurs, which could be a client problem or a server
problem. Most errors are recoverable and the session will stay open, we
recommend to implementors to monitor and log error messages by default.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

type.description: The event type, must be `error`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferC.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferCleared
RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferC.description:
Returned when the input audio buffer is cleared by the client with a
`input_audio_buffer.clear` event.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

type.description: The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.cleared`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferC.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferCommitted
RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferC.description:
Returned when an input audio buffer is committed, either by the client or
automatically in server VAD mode. The `item_id` property is the ID of the user
message item that will be created, thus a `conversation.item.created` event
will also be sent to the client.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the server event.

item_id.description: The ID of the user message item that will be created.

type.description: The event type, must be `input_audio_buffer.committed`.

RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferS.title: RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferSpeechStarted
RealtimeBetaServerEventInputAudioBufferS.description:
Sent by the server when in `server_vad` mode to indicate that speech has been
detected in the audio buffer. This can happen any time audio is added to the
buffer (unless speech is already detected). The client may want to use this
event to interrupt audio playback or provide visual feedback to the user.

The client should expect to receive a `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event
when speech stops. The `item_id` property is the ID of the user message item
that will be created when speech stops and will also be included in the
`input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` event (unless the client manually commits
the audio buffer during VAD activation).

audio_start_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the start of all audio written to the buffer during the
session when speech was first detected. This will correspond to the
beginning of audio sent to the model, and thus includes the
